title: Measuring social bias in knowledge graph embeddings
benchmark_measurement: Stereotypical associations between professions and religious groups (specifically Catholicism vs. Islam) encoded in knowledge graph embeddings.
findings: The knowledge graph embeddings were found to encode strong stereotypical associations between professions and religious identities. For example, professions like 'Catholic priest' and 'bishop' were highly associated with Catholicism, while 'imam' and 'muhaddith' were highly associated with Islam. This demonstrates that statistical imbalances in the training data (Wikidata and FB3M) are learned by the embedding models, resulting in measurable religious bias.
